entities.summary:
André Dias de Escobar (born unknown, died 1448) was a Portuguese Benedictine theologian.

He wrote extensively on the nature of God and the human condition, influencing the development of scholastic theology in Europe during the late Middle Ages. His works were widely read and studied by scholars such as Thomas Aquinas and Duns Scotus.

De Escobar's theology was marked by a strong emphasis on reason and intellectual inquiry, which set him apart from other theologians of his time. This emphasis helped shape the intellectual landscape of the Renaissance era to come.

The legacy of André Dias de Escobar can be seen in the many theologians and scholars who followed in his footsteps, including John Duns Scotus and William of Ockham.

André Dias de Escobar's most famous quote is 'Veritas odium parit,' or 'Truth begets hatred.'
